narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is being 'mindful of frail man' and the type (102) is cognition: the reading treats mindfulness here not as an emotion but as an act of the mind holding another in view. Uniquely, the mind held is God's, and the wonder is the psalmist's; the bearer (105) is the psalmist and the operation (106) is that, confronted with the vast heavens, the self marvels that God is mindful of and cares for so small a creature as man. Source (103) is absent (present:false): the text supplies no prior cause for the wonder beyond the sight of the sky itself, so the movement reads as spontaneous, triggered by contemplation rather than by any inner antecedent. Seat (104) is explicitly 'none' - the operation is not lodged in any organ (no heart, no kidneys); it is a whole-self astonishment, not an organ-function. The target (107) is 'humbled-wonder' and the coupling (112) is the very question 'why-mindful-of-man', so the process runs: contemplation of vastness -> awareness of own smallness -> astonishment at being noticed -> humbled wonder. Manner (108) is 'none' and intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are all absent: the reading records no stated style, no measured degree, no downstream consequence - the wonder is left as a standing interior posture rather than issuing in an act. The discovery note (114) fixes it in v4: the interior weighs its own smallness against the star-filled sky and is astonished at being noticed at all. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state and role (115) is characteristic: this is a genuine inner-being movement, God's mindfulness the arena the self measures itself against, and the finding is the self-diminishment-in-wonder that God's attention provokes.
narratives.story: Standing under a night sky full of stars, the poet is struck by how tiny a human being is against all that vastness - and yet God keeps human beings in mind and cares for them. The poem gives no reason for this wonder except the sky itself; the feeling simply rises when he looks up. It is not lodged in any one part of him but seizes the whole person as a kind of humbled amazement. Nothing is said about how strongly he feels it or what he then does; the wonder is left standing on its own. What the passage shows is a self shrinking in astonishment precisely because it discovers it is noticed.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'the nations remember and worship' and the type (102) is affect - notably NOT cognition here: the remembering is read as an affective turning, not a bare recollection. The bearer (105) is 'the nations' (not the psalmist), which is the distinctive mark of this reading among the 'remember' set: the interior movement is universalised, carried by all peoples rather than by the single sufferer. Source (103) is absent: no inner cause is named; the operation (106) supplies the external trigger - the one man's vindication spreading to the peoples so that all the ends of the earth remember and turn to the LORD. Seat (104) is 'none' - the turning is not organ-located but a whole-people reorientation. Target (107) is 'universal-turning' and coupling (112) is 'nations-remember': the process runs rescue-of-the-one -> memory awakened in the many -> turning and worship. Manner (108) is 'none', and intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) are all absent: the reading does not measure the fervour or trace a consequence beyond the worship itself. The discovery note (114) reads v27 as the operation universalising the psalm: the one man's rescue draws the nations' interior back to God. Role (115) is characteristic and locus (116) internal:ib-state: within the human inner life this is memory functioning as the hinge of conversion - to remember God is to turn to him, the two named as one motion.
narratives.story: Here the poet imagines that the rescue of one suffering man will ripple outward until people everywhere call God to mind and turn to worship him. This remembering is less a cold act of recall than a warm turning of the whole self back toward God. It is carried not by one person but by all the nations, so the private deliverance becomes a public homecoming. The poem does not measure how deeply they feel it or what follows; it simply names remembering and turning as a single movement. The striking thing is that memory here is the very doorway to conversion.
narratives.variation_note: Against the other 'remember' readings (mostly the psalmist recalling God in distress), this one is borne by 'the nations', typed as affect not cognition, and located as universal-turning: the bearer shifts from the single sufferer to all peoples, and remembrance becomes corporate conversion rather than private recall.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember not my youth's sins' and the type (102) is cognition. This reading is distinctive because the operation (106) is a plea about God's remembering, not the psalmist's own: the self asks God NOT to remember the sins of its youth but to remember it by steadfast love - a penitent appeal for a divine forgetting. The bearer (105) is the psalmist, and the movement is inward petition directed outward to God. Source (103) is absent: no prior inner state is named as cause; the penitence stands as the given posture. Seat (104) is 'none' - not organ-located; it is the whole penitent self appealing. Target (107) is 'penitence' and coupling (112) is 'remember-not-sins': the process runs guilt-consciousness -> plea for the record to be blotted -> request that love, not sin, be the lens of God's memory. Manner (108) is 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree, no consequence traced, the appeal left open. The discovery note (114) reads v7 as a penitent's plea: let the record of old sin be blotted, and let love be the lens instead. Role (115) is characteristic, locus (116) internal:ib-state: as an inner-being movement this is memory used morally - the self petitioning for selective divine memory, wanting to be remembered under mercy and forgotten under judgement.
narratives.story: The poet begs God not to hold the sins of his younger years against him, but to keep him in mind through love instead. It is the prayer of a person conscious of guilt, asking that the old record be wiped and that mercy, not failure, be the way God sees him. Nothing is said about how intense the feeling is or what comes of it; the plea is simply left with God. The heart of it is a wish for a kind of chosen forgetting - to be remembered kindly and forgotten in one's faults.
narratives.variation_note: Unlike the readings where the psalmist himself remembers, here the psalmist asks GOD to remember-not: remembrance is inverted into a petition for divine forgetting of sin, the target being penitence rather than recall of God's deeds.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'in prosperity, I shall never be moved' and the type (102) is cognition: the reading treats the confident 'never' as a thought the self once held. The bearer (105) is the psalmist and the operation (106) is that the self recalls that in its ease it presumed it would never be moved - the complacency of good times, now confessed. Source (103) is absent: the text names no deeper cause than the prosperity itself, so the false security reads as bred simply by comfort. Seat (104) is 'none' - the complacency is not organ-located; it is a whole-self settled assumption. Target (107) is 'complacency' and coupling (112) is 'never-be-moved': the process runs prosperity -> lulled interior -> presumption of permanence -> (implicitly, by the psalm's turn) exposure when God hides his face. Manner (108) is 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - the reading does not grade the complacency or trace its collapse here, though the surrounding verses supply it. The discovery note (114) reads v6 as naming a past over-confidence: prosperity had lulled the interior into a false sense of permanence. Role (115) is characteristic, locus (116) internal:ib-state. Read without valence-bias, this is a dark inner movement narrated honestly: security misread as self-sufficiency, the 'never' of a heart that mistook God's favour for its own unshakeable standing.
narratives.story: Looking back, the poet remembers how, when life was easy, he told himself nothing could ever shake him. It was the quiet over-confidence that good times breed - security mistaken for permanence, with no deeper cause than comfort itself. The poem does not spell out here how the fall came, only names the smugness for what it was. It is an honest confession of a heart that took ease for granted and assumed it would always stand.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'forgotten like one who is dead' and the type (102) is state - not an action but a condition suffered. This is the distinctive note of the reading: the psalmist is the object, not the agent, of forgetting. The bearer (105) is the psalmist and the operation (106) is that the self has been forgotten like a dead man, become like a broken vessel - the sense of being erased and discarded. Source (103) is absent: no cause is named for the erasure; it is simply the social fact pressing on the interior. Seat (104) is 'none' - the felt erasure is not organ-located but a whole-self experience of oblivion. Target (107) is 'erasure' and coupling (112) is 'forgotten-like-dead': the process runs being-forgotten-by-others -> inward sense of having dropped out of memory -> self-perception as useless, a broken vessel. Manner (108) is 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - the reading does not grade the desolation or name a consequence, leaving it as raw condition. The discovery note (114) distinguishes it from being merely shunned: this is the sense of having dropped out of memory entirely, useless and cast aside. Role (115) is characteristic, locus (116) internal:ib-state. As an inner-being movement this is the passive face of the memory-family: to be forgotten is experienced as a kind of death, the self annihilated in others' minds.
narratives.story: The poet feels as though everyone has forgotten him, the way people forget the dead - he has become like a jar that is broken and thrown out. No reason is given; it is simply the crushing sense of having dropped completely out of other people's minds, useless and discarded. This is different from merely being avoided: it is the feeling of being erased altogether. The passage shows that to be forgotten can be lived as a kind of death.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember (zakar - these things)' and the type (102) is action: a deliberate recollection. The bearer (105) is David and the operation (106) is simply 'remember', but its object is set by the target (107): the past worship in the throng. The distinctive mark here is the manner (108), which is not 'none' but a genuine pairing - 'pouring out his soul' (item_type pair, spanning the recollection) - so the memory is enacted amid grief, not in calm. Source (103) is absent and coupling (112) is 'none': the reading declines to name an inner cause or a further inner link, isolating the bare act of recall bound only to the outpouring. Seat (104) is 'none' - not organ-located. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent: no degree or consequence recorded, though the note supplies the emotional colour. The discovery note (114) reads it as memory of past worship deepening present grief: this zakar (first of two, vv4,6) is the recollection of festal joy that now pains the exile. Role (115) is characteristic, locus (116) internal:ib-state. As an inner-being movement, memory here works against the self: recalling former nearness to God sharpens the ache of present distance - remembrance as wound.
narratives.story: Far from the temple, the poet remembers how he used to walk with the festival crowds to God's house amid shouts of joy - and the memory is bittersweet, remembered as he pours out his grief. The recollection is deliberate, but it does not comfort; recalling that lost happiness only deepens the pain of being cut off now. The poem names no cause and traces no outcome, just the act of remembering bound to the weeping. Here memory cuts rather than heals.
narratives.variation_note: This first zakar of Psalm 42 differs from its pair in v6: here the object is past worship (locus internal:ib-state) and the memory WOUNDS - the manner 'pouring out his soul' binds recall to grief; in v6 the object is God himself and memory turns redemptive.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember (zakar - you, from afar)' and the type (102) is action. The bearer (105) is David; the operation (106) is 'remember' and the target (107) is God himself ('you') - this is the decisive difference from its pair in v4, where the object was past worship. The locus (116) is external:god (not internal:ib-state), marking that the memory reaches out toward God as its object. Manner (108) is 'from the land of Jordan and Hermon' - memory exercised in exile, at the far edge of the land. Source (103) is absent, but coupling (112) is a pairing, 'driven by the cast-down soul' (span-linked to the downcast self of v5-6): so the process runs dejection -> the cast-down soul turning -> Godward remembrance from the far country. Seat (104) is 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree or outcome measured. The discovery note (114) reads it as memory turned Godward from exile: the redemptive remembering of God himself from the far-off land, hope's anchor in dejection. Role (115) is characteristic, locus external:god. As an inner-being movement this is memory reversing the wound of v4: the same faculty that sharpened grief now, aimed at God rather than at lost joy, becomes the tether of hope.
narratives.story: From a distant land, cast down and low, the poet turns and calls God himself to mind. Unlike his earlier memory of happier days, this remembering reaches out toward God, and it steadies rather than saddens him - it is his anchor when everything feels far away. It rises straight out of his downcast state, the sinking soul turning upward. The same act of memory that had deepened his grief now, aimed at God, becomes his hope.
narratives.variation_note: Paired with v4: the object shifts from past worship to God himself and the locus from internal:ib-state to external:god, so the SAME faculty that wounded in v4 here becomes redemptive - memory Godward is hope, memory of lost joy is grief. The difference in target carries the whole meaning.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'forget (shakach - not forgotten you)' and the type (102) is action. Distinctively, this reading carries an explicit prohibition dimension (113): 'negated (we have NOT forgotten you)' - the only place a prohibition flag fires in this set. The bearer (105) is 'the nation' and the operation (106) is 'forget (negated)', targeting God ('you', 107). Locus (116) is external:god. Source (103) is absent; seat (104) is 'none' - the fidelity is not organ-located but a corporate posture. Coupling (112) is a pairing, 'paired with not being false to covenant' (span-linked), so the process runs undeserved suffering -> protest of innocence -> the double denial: we have not forgotten you AND we have not broken covenant. Manner (108) is 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - the reading does not grade the loyalty or name a consequence. The discovery note (114) reads it as the protest of innocence: undeserved suffering despite fidelity, the nation insisting it has not abandoned God - the anguish of the faithful afflicted. Role (115) is characteristic, locus external:god. As an inner-being movement this is memory as maintained fidelity under undeserved blows: not-forgetting held up as evidence against the apparent verdict of their suffering.
narratives.story: Struck down and shamed, the whole people protest that they have done nothing to deserve it: they have not forgotten God, nor been false to their agreement with him. The remembering here is loyalty held firm - a corporate refusal to abandon God even while he seems to have abandoned them. It is stated flatly as a denial: we have NOT forgotten. This is the anguish of the faithful who suffer anyway, holding up their unbroken memory as proof of their innocence.
narratives.variation_note: Among the 'forgotten' readings this alone fires a prohibition flag (explicit negation) and is borne corporately by 'the nation': forgetting is denied as a claim of innocence, contrasting the passive erasure of Psa 31:12 and the hypothetical apostasy of the paired v20.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'forget (shakach - if we had forgotten God)' and the type (102) is action. The distinctive mark is that the bearer (105) is 'the nation (hypothetically)' and the operation (106) is 'forget (hypothetical)': this is forgetting entertained as a supposition, not confessed or denied outright but imagined as a test case. The target (107) is 'the name of our God'; locus (116) external:god. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none'; coupling (112) 'none' - the reading isolates the hypothetical, unlinked to any other inner motion. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree, no traced consequence, because the act never actually occurs. Unlike its pair in v17, here there is no prohibition flag: the negation there was a denial, here the frame is conditional ('if'). The discovery note (114) reads it as the hypothetical apostasy the nation denies: the imagined betrayal that would have justified judgement - but God who knows the heart would have found them true. Role (115) is characteristic, locus external:god. As an inner-being movement this is forgetting-as-thought-experiment: the nation submits its own interior to God's scrutiny, confident that even the searcher of hearts would find no forgetting there.
narratives.story: The people put a hard question to themselves: if we HAD forgotten God, or turned to some foreign god, wouldn't God know? He sees the secrets of every heart. Here forgetting is imagined rather than admitted - a test they are sure they would pass, since God can read them through and through. It is the opposite of the real forgetting elsewhere in the poem: an offered self-examination, confident that the searcher of hearts would find them loyal.
narratives.variation_note: Paired with v17: v17 flatly DENIES forgetting (prohibition flag), while v20 entertains it HYPOTHETICALLY ('if we had') with no prohibition flag and coupling 'none' - the shift from denial to supposition is the finding, both submitting the interior to God who knows the heart.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'forget (shakach - forget your people)' and the type (102) is action. This reading is distinctive in the whole family: forgetting is COMMANDED and GOOD. The bearer (105) is 'the bride (daughter)' and the operation (106) is 'forget', with target (107) 'your people and father's house' - a deliberate inward leaving of former ties. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state. Source (103) is absent; seat (104) 'none' - the forsaking is not organ-located but a whole-self reorientation of loyalty. Coupling (112) is a pairing, 'so the king will desire her beauty' (span-linked to the reward): the process runs summons ('hear, consider, incline your ear') -> deliberate forgetting of old loyalties -> cleaving to the king -> being desired. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured, the consequence named only via the coupling, not as a separate effect row. The discovery note (114) reads it as the bride's inward leaving of her old ties: the deliberate forsaking of former loyalties to cleave to the king, the cost and turn of covenant union. Role (115) is characteristic, locus internal:ib-state. As an inner-being movement this shows forgetting with positive valence - not decay but chosen release, memory-loss as the price and gateway of a new bond.
narratives.story: The bride is told to listen and take it to heart: forget your own people and your father's house, and the king will delight in you. Here forgetting is not a failure but a command and a good thing - a deliberate letting-go of old loyalties so she can give herself wholly to her new lord. It is a chosen release, the whole self turning from what it was bound to before. The passage shows the surprising other side of forgetting: sometimes leaving the past behind is exactly what love requires.
narratives.variation_note: Against the other 'forget' readings (where forgetting God/his works is the sin), here forgetting is COMMANDED and positively valenced - the bride forgetting her father's house to cleave to the king; the target is human ties, not God, and the coupling makes the forgetting the gateway to union rather than to ruin.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember / make remembered (zakar, hiphil - your name)' and the type (102) is action. The distinctive grammar is causative: the operation (106) is 'cause to be remembered', so the psalmist does not merely recall but actively perpetuates. The bearer (105) is the psalmist and the target (107) is the king's name, in all generations. The locus (116) is external:person - the only reading in the set aimed at a human object rather than God or the psalmist's own state. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) is a pairing, 'paired with the nations' praise' (span-linked): the process runs the poet's vow -> making the king's name remembered -> the nations praising him forever. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree, the outcome carried by the coupling. The discovery note (114) reads it as the poet's vow to perpetuate the king's renown: the making-remembered of the king's name so the nations praise him forever. Role (115) is characteristic, locus external:person. As an inner-being movement this is memory turned outward and productive: the self commits itself to keeping another's name alive, remembrance as an act of tribute that generates worship in others.
narratives.story: The poet promises to keep the king's name alive for all future generations, so that nations will praise him forever. This is not private recall but active memory-making - a vow to carry another person's renown down the ages. It is bound to the praise it will produce: because the poet perpetuates the name, others will honour it endlessly. Here remembering is directed at a human figure and becomes a deliberate act of tribute.
narratives.variation_note: Distinct among 'remember' readings: the verb is causative ('make remembered') and the locus is external:person (the king), not God or the self - remembrance here is outward tribute that generates others' praise, rather than the self recalling God in distress.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'forget (shakach - you who forget God)' and the type (102) is action. This reading is unique in the set for carrying a SOURCE dimension (103): 'emboldened by God's silence at their sin (v21)' (item_type pair, span-linked) - the only reading where an inner/situational cause of the movement is actually named. The bearer (105) is 'the God-forgetters' and the operation (106) is 'forget', targeting God (107); locus (116) external:god. Seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) is a pairing, 'warned to consider' (span-linked): the process runs God's silence at sin -> the presumption that God is 'one like yourself' -> forgetting God -> the standing warning 'lest I tear you apart'. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - the reading does not grade the sin or name a downstream effect beyond the threat carried in the coupling. The discovery note (114) reads it as the root of the wicked's sin: God-forgetfulness, emboldened by his silence, the deadly presumption that draws the warning. Role (115) is characteristic, locus external:god. Read without valence-bias, this is the family's darkest specimen given a diagnosis: forgetting God is not accident but presumption bred by mistaking his patience for indifference - the wicked's interior traced to its cause.
narratives.story: God turns to the wicked and warns them: you who forget me, take heed, or I will tear you apart with none to rescue. And the poem tells us why they forget - because God stayed silent while they sinned, they assumed he was just like them and stopped taking him seriously. So their forgetting is no innocent lapse; it is presumption bred by mistaking God's patience for weakness. It is the deadly root of their whole way of life, and it draws a grave warning.
narratives.variation_note: Unique among 'forget' readings for a stated SOURCE ('emboldened by God's silence at their sin'): where other forgettings are simply reported, here the wicked's God-forgetfulness is DIAGNOSED as presumption bred by mistaking God's patience for indifference.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'forget (shakach - lest my people forget)' and the type (102) is status. Distinctively, the forgetting here is a DANGER TO BE PREVENTED, not an act performed: the operation (106) is 'forget (the danger to be avoided)' (resolution inferred). The bearer (105) is 'the psalmist's people' and the target (107) is God's judgment / lesson; locus (116) internal:ib-state. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) is a pairing, 'the reason God is asked to make them totter rather than kill outright' (span-linked): the process runs threat-of-forgetting -> plea that judgement be lingering not swift -> the wicked made to totter as a standing warning so memory endures. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured. The discovery note (114) reads it as a lingering judgment sought so the lesson endures: the people must not lose sight of God's justice, so the wicked are made to totter rather than swept away at once. Role (115) is characteristic, locus internal:ib-state. As an inner-being movement this is memory governing the shape of justice itself: the fear that the people's memory of God's judgement will fade drives a request that the punishment be visibly prolonged - forgetting pre-empted by design.
narratives.story: The poet asks God not to kill his enemies outright but to make them stagger and fall slowly - and the reason is memory. If they were destroyed all at once, the people might soon forget the lesson; but a lingering, visible judgment stays before their eyes. So the danger here is not a forgetting that has happened but one that must be prevented. The poem shows memory shaping even how justice should be carried out, so that the people never lose sight of God's justice.
narratives.variation_note: Distinct from the enacted forgettings: here forgetting is a status/DANGER TO BE AVOIDED (not a deed done), and it drives the shape of judgement - a lingering punishment is requested precisely so the people will NOT forget God's justice.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember (zakar - when I remember you upon my bed)' and the type (102) is action. The bearer (105) is the psalmist and the operation (106) is 'remember / call to mind', with target (107) God; locus (116) external:god. The distinctive mark is the manner (108): 'upon his bed, in the night' - remembrance located in the wakeful dark. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) is a pairing, 'paired with meditating in the night watches' (span-linked): the process runs nightfall -> the mind turned Godward on the bed -> meditation through the watches -> the joy of v5-7. Manner is thus temporal and postural rather than emotional-graded. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree, the effect carried by the coupling into the singing of v7. The discovery note (114) reads it as God the last thought of the wakeful night: the calling of God to mind in the dark hours, memory feeding the joy of v5. Role (115) is characteristic, locus external:god. As an inner-being movement this is memory as sustained nocturnal communion: the mind turned Godward when the world is still, and remembrance here nourishes satisfaction rather than grief - the calm counterpart to Psalm 77's night-remembering that moaned.
narratives.story: Lying awake at night, the poet turns his thoughts to God and dwells on him through the dark hours. Here remembering is a quiet, sustained companionship in the stillness, the mind resting on God when everything else is silent. Far from troubling him, it feeds a deep contentment - the memory flows into praise and joyful singing. It is the peaceful side of night-time remembering: God as the last and best thought before sleep.
narratives.variation_note: A night-remembering like Psa 77:3/77:6, but here (manner 'upon his bed, in the night', coupled with meditation) memory NOURISHES joy rather than deepening the groan - the calm inverse of 77's anguished night-recall.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remind / make mention (zakar - I will remind them of your righteousness)' and the type (102) is action. This is the family's outward-facing specimen: the operation (106) is 'remind / make mention' - memory spoken to others, not held privately. The bearer (105) is the psalmist; the target (107) is 'God's righteousness, his alone' (item_type pair, span-linked, the exclusivity built in); locus (116) external:god. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Manner (108) is a pairing, 'coming with the mighty deeds of the Lord GOD' (span-linked), and coupling (112) another pairing, 'paired with telling and proclaiming God's deeds' (span-linked): the process runs the aged witness -> coming armed with God's mighty deeds -> making mention of God's righteousness ONLY -> testimony that all saving deeds are God's, not his own. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree, the effect being the testimony itself. The discovery note (114) reads it as testimony that God's righteousness stands alone: the making-mention of God's righteousness only, the aged witness insisting all saving deeds are God's, not his own. Role (115) is characteristic, locus external:god. As an inner-being movement this is memory as public confession: the interior act of recalling God's righteousness turned into speech that credits God exclusively - remembrance as self-effacing witness.
narratives.story: Grown old, the poet vows to go out proclaiming God's mighty deeds and to make mention of God's righteousness - and his alone. Here remembering is spoken aloud to others rather than kept inside; it is testimony. The whole point is that he insists none of the saving deeds are his own doing but God's entirely. His memory becomes a public confession that gives all the credit to God.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember (zakar - I remember God and moan)' and the type (102) is action. The bearer (105) is the psalmist and the operation (106) is 'remember / call to mind', target (107) God; locus (116) external:god. The distinctive mark is the manner (108): 'with moaning' (item_type pair, span-linked) - the remembering does not soothe but is accompanied by a groan. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) is a pairing, 'paired with moaning and the fainting spirit' (span-linked): the process runs distress -> remembering God -> moaning -> the spirit fainting under meditation. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured, the effect carried by the coupling into the fainting spirit. The discovery note (114) names the paradox that memory of God brings not solace but anguish here: zakar in the distress-phase, remembrance that deepens the groan rather than lifting it (contrast v11 where remembering becomes the turn to hope). Role (115) is characteristic, locus external:god. As an inner-being movement this is the wounding face of Godward memory: calling God to mind in the night intensifies the pain because God seems to have changed - the same faculty that will later heal here only deepens the groan.
narratives.story: When the poet calls God to mind, he does not find comfort - he groans, and as he broods his spirit sinks. Remembering God, which we expect to help, here only sharpens the pain, because God now seems distant and changed. The memory comes wrapped in moaning and a fainting spirit. It is the wounding side of thinking about God: in this dark stretch, recalling him deepens the ache rather than easing it.
narratives.variation_note: The first pole of Psalm 77's memory-arc: here remembering God WOUNDS (manner 'with moaning', spirit fainting), the deliberate contrast to vv6/11 where the same act of memory becomes the deliberate turn to hope. The variation across one psalm is the finding.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember (zakar - I will remember the deeds of the LORD)' and the type (102) is action. This is the hinge of the psalm: the operation (106) is 'remember / recall deliberately', an act of resolved will. The bearer (105) is the psalmist; the target (107) is 'the deeds and wonders of the LORD' (item_type pair, span-linked). Locus (116) external:god. The distinctive mark is the manner (108): 'resolved, deliberate (I will)' - memory chosen, not merely suffered. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) is a pairing, 'paired with the second remember and the pondering' (span-linked): the process runs despairing questions (vv7-9) -> the decisive 'I will remember' -> recalling God's works -> steadied faith. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - the reading does not grade the resolve, though it is marked as decisive. The discovery note (114) reads it as the decisive act of will that turns the psalm: memory chosen as remedy, the sufferer deliberately recalling God's works to answer his own despairing questions - remembrance now healing where in v3 it wounded. Role (115) is characteristic, locus external:god. As an inner-being movement this is memory as chosen medicine: the will deliberately turning to God's past deeds to overturn present despair - the healing pole opposite v3's wound.
narratives.story: At his lowest, questioning whether God's love has failed forever, the poet makes a deliberate choice: 'I will remember the deeds of the LORD.' Here remembering is an act of will, a decision to recall God's past works in order to answer his own despairing doubts. Where earlier remembering only made him groan, now it becomes his cure. This is memory chosen on purpose as a remedy, the turning-point of the whole poem.
narratives.variation_note: The healing pole of Psalm 77's arc and the psalm's hinge: manner 'resolved, deliberate (I will)' - memory CHOSEN as remedy, directly reversing v3 where remembrance wounded. Paired with remember#9 (the doubled resolve) which it span-links to.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember (zakar - I will remember your wonders)' and the type (102) is action. This is the SECOND remember of v11, the doubling of the resolve. The bearer (105) is the psalmist; the target (107) is 'your wonders of old' (item_type pair, span-linked). Locus (116) external:god. The distinctive mark is the manner (108): 'emphatic repetition (yes, I will remember)' - memory pressed home by repetition. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) is a pairing, 'paired with the first resolve to remember' (span-linked to remember#8): the process runs decision -> doubled affirmation -> the will fixed on God's ancient wonders (the Exodus, vv16-20). Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - the emphasis is registered in manner, not as a graded intensity. The discovery note (114) reads it as the doubled resolve, memory pressed home: zakar repeated to fix the will on God's ancient wonders, the deliberate rehearsal that steadies faith. Role (115) is characteristic, locus external:god. Preserving the distinction from remember#8 (directive 8): the two are not one act - the first is the decision, the second its emphatic reinforcement; the difference is the deliberate rehearsal, memory fixing itself by repeating itself.
narratives.story: Having resolved to remember God's deeds, the poet says it again, more firmly: 'yes, I will remember your wonders of old.' The repetition is the point - by saying it twice he presses the memory home and fixes his mind on God's ancient rescues, above all the Exodus. It is a deliberate rehearsal, memory strengthening itself by dwelling and insisting. Faith is steadied here not by one recollection but by pressing it home again.
narratives.variation_note: The doubled second half of v11's resolve (paired with remember#8): distinguished by manner 'emphatic repetition (yes, I will remember)' - not the decision itself but its reinforcement; the difference between deciding and pressing-home is preserved as the finding (directive 8).

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember (zakar - I remember my song in the night)' and the type (102) is action. The bearer (105) is the psalmist and the operation (106) is 'remember / recall'; the target (107) is 'my song in the night' - a former melody of praise, not God directly, so the locus (116) is internal:ib-state. The distinctive mark is the manner (108): 'meditating in the heart' (item_type pair, span-linked) - recall paired with inward brooding. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) is a pairing, 'paired with meditating and the spirit's search' (span-linked): the process runs sleepless night -> recalling a happier song -> meditation -> the spirit's diligent search for what is lost. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent. The discovery note (114) reads it as recalling former nights of praise now turned to grief: the memory of a happier melody, summoned in the sleepless dark as the heart searches for what was lost. Role (115) is characteristic, locus internal:ib-state. As an inner-being movement this stands between the psalm's poles: memory of a past song is summoned, but it drives a searching, questioning brooding (the doubting vv7-9) before the resolve of v11 - remembrance as the restless probe that precedes the decisive turn.
narratives.story: Unable to sleep, the poet recalls a song he used to sing in happier nights, and turns it over in his heart. But the memory of that lost gladness does not settle him; it sets his spirit searching, asking whether God has abandoned him for good. Here remembering opens a restless probing rather than peace. It is the searching stage that comes just before he chooses, later, to remember God's deeds and find his footing again.
narratives.variation_note: Distinct within Psalm 77: the object is 'my song in the night' (locus internal:ib-state), not God's deeds - memory here drives the spirit's restless SEARCH (vv7-9) that stands between the wounding recall of v3 and the healing resolve of v11.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'forget (shakach, negated)' and the type (102) is disposition - a settled orientation rather than a single act. The bearer (105) is 'the children', the coming generation, and the operation (106) is 'refuse to forget', target (107) 'the works of God'. Locus (116) internal:ib-state. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) is 'paired with hope and obedience' (inferred): the process runs the fathers' teaching -> the children setting their hope in God -> NOT forgetting his works -> keeping his commandments. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured, the outcome (obedience) carried by the coupling. The discovery note (114) reads it as the guarded memory, the safeguard against the fathers' fatal amnesia (v11). Role (115) is characteristic, locus internal:ib-state. As an inner-being movement this is memory as intergenerational safeguard: not-forgetting cultivated as a disposition by teaching, so that remembrance, hope, and obedience form a single chain - the deliberate remedy set against the forgetting that ruined the fathers.
narratives.story: The whole point of teaching the next generation, the poem says, is so that the children will set their hope in God and not forget what he has done, but keep his commands. Here not-forgetting is a settled attitude to be cultivated, passed down deliberately so that it becomes second nature. Remembering, hope, and obedience hang together as one chain. It is set up as the safeguard against the very forgetting that had ruined the fathers.
narratives.variation_note: A NOT-forget disposition (borne by 'the children', coupled with hope and obedience), set deliberately against the enacted forgetting of the fathers narrated in the same psalm (forgot#1, v11) - memory cultivated as safeguard rather than lost.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'forget (shakach)' and the type (102) is action - here an accomplished deed, past tense. The bearer (105) is 'the fathers' and the operation (106) is 'forget', target (107) 'God's works and wonders'. Locus (116) internal:ib-state. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) is 'paired with the wonders no longer believed' (inferred): the process runs covenant broken, law refused (vv10) -> forgetting God's works -> the wonders no longer believed. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured, the consequence carried by the coupling. The discovery note (114) reads it as the forgetting the prologue warned of, now realized in the fathers. Role (115) is characteristic, locus internal:ib-state. Read without valence-bias, this is the negative fulfilment set against the teaching of v7: what the children were to be trained to avoid, the fathers actually did. As an inner-being movement, forgetting here is the interior root of apostasy - the works and wonders dropping out of mind, and with them faith itself.
narratives.story: The poem turns to the fathers and states plainly what went wrong: they forgot God's works and the wonders he had shown them. This is forgetting as an accomplished failure, the exact thing the children were later to be taught to avoid. Once the mighty deeds slipped from their minds, they no longer believed them, and they broke covenant. Here forgetting is the inner root of falling away - lose the memory, and faith goes with it.
narratives.variation_note: The enacted, past-tense forgetting of the fathers (type action) - the negative fulfilment answering the NOT-forget disposition the children are taught in the same psalm (forget#4, v7): what they were to avoid, the fathers did.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember (zakar)' and the type (102) is action. The bearer (105) is 'they' - the people under judgement - and the operation (106) is 'remember', target (107) 'that God was their rock'. Locus (116) external:god. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) is 'paired with the flattering that followed' (inferred): the process runs God's killing stroke (v31,34) -> the people seeking and repenting -> remembering God as their rock and redeemer -> BUT flattery and lies (v36). Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - the reading does not grade the sincerity, but the coupling exposes it as short-lived. The discovery note (114) reads it as the memory jogged by judgement, but only for a moment. Role (115) is characteristic, locus external:god. As an inner-being movement this is memory as fear-driven and shallow: judgement forces recollection of who God is, but the coupling to the flattering that follows shows the remembrance did not reach the will - a memory that recalled the truth without changing the heart.
narratives.story: When God struck them down, the people turned back and remembered that he was their rock and rescuer. But the memory was shallow: the very next moment they were flattering him with their mouths and lying with their tongues. Here remembering is jogged by fear of judgment, real enough to name the truth but too thin to change them. It shows that recalling who God is can happen without the heart being moved at all.
narratives.variation_note: A fear-driven, SHALLOW remembering: unlike the deliberate faith-recall of Psa 77:11 or 143:5, this memory is jogged by judgement and immediately betrayed by flattery (coupling) - remembrance that names the truth without reaching the will.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember (zakar, negated)' and the type (102) is action. This is a NOT-remember: the operation (106) is 'fail to remember'. The bearer (105) is 'they' and the target (107) is 'his power and redemption'. Locus (116) internal:ib-state. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) is 'paired with the deeds of the Exodus they forgot' (inferred): the process runs unsteady heart (v37) -> failing to remember God's power and the day of redemption -> the whole Exodus recital (vv43-46) being precisely what was forgotten. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent. The discovery note (114) reads it as forgetfulness of the very deliverance, the recital that follows being what they forgot. Role (115) is characteristic, locus internal:ib-state. As an inner-being movement this is memory-failure as ingratitude toward salvation itself: not merely forgetting facts but failing to hold on to the day of their own rescue - the psalm then rehearsing at length the plagues and the parting of the sea, as if to supply the memory the people would not keep.
narratives.story: The poem charges the people with failing to remember God's power and the day he redeemed them from their enemies. This is a not-remembering - the mind letting go of the very rescue that had saved them. To drive it home, the psalm then recites in detail the plagues and wonders in Egypt, laying out exactly what they had forgotten. Here memory-failure is ingratitude toward salvation itself: they could not keep hold of the day they were set free.
narratives.variation_note: A NOT-remember (fail to remember his power/redemption), the counterpart within Psalm 78 to the shallow remembering of v35 - here memory fails entirely toward the Exodus, which the psalm then recites as the very content they let slip.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'forget (shakach)' and the type (102) is state - a condition of affliction, not a moral act. This reading is distinctive: the thing forgotten is not God but bread. The bearer (105) is the psalmist and the operation (106) is 'forget to eat', target (107) 'his bread'. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) here carries an odd datum, 'internal:ib-state' (a locus-value lodged in the coupling row), and locus (116) reads 'paired with the withered heart' - the two dimensions appear transposed in the record, but together they bind the forgetting to the struck-down, withered heart of v4. The process runs grief -> heart withered like grass -> the body's needs falling from mind -> forgetting even to eat. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured. The discovery note (114) reads v4 as the loss of appetite in deep grief, affliction that consumes even hunger. Role (115) is characteristic. As an inner-being movement this is forgetting as the body-effect of sorrow: grief so total that it erases the most basic self-maintenance - memory-loss here is not sin or safeguard but a symptom, the interior so consumed that it forgets to keep itself alive.
narratives.story: The poet is so crushed by grief that he forgets even to eat his bread; his heart is struck down and withered like dried grass. Here forgetting is not a moral failure but a symptom of sorrow - affliction so deep it swallows up ordinary hunger. It is bound to the withered heart, the whole self consumed by pain. This shows that grief can be total enough to make a person forget to keep himself alive.
narratives.variation_note: Unique among 'forget' readings: the object is bread, not God/his works, and the type is state (a symptom of grief), not sin - forgetting here is the body-effect of sorrow, memory-loss as affliction rather than fault.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'forget (shakach, negated)' and the type (102) is disposition. The operation (106) is 'not forget', a self-command in worship. The bearer (105) is the psalmist, addressing his own soul, and the target (107) is 'all God's benefits'. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. As in forget#5, the record shows the locus/coupling datum transposed: coupling (112) reads 'internal:ib-state' and locus (116) reads 'paired with blessing the LORD' - together binding the not-forgetting to the summons 'Bless the LORD, O my soul'. The process runs the soul addressed -> the command to bless -> and NOT to forget God's benefits (forgiveness, healing, redemption, crowning love, vv3-4). Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured, the benefits themselves supplying the content. The discovery note (114) reads v2 as the guarded memory of God's goodness, worship that refuses amnesia. Role (115) is characteristic. As an inner-being movement this is memory as the engine of praise: the self commanding itself not to let God's benefits slip from mind, so that remembrance and blessing are one act - gratitude sustained by a deliberate refusal to forget.
narratives.story: The poet turns to his own soul and charges it: bless the LORD, and do not forget all his benefits - his forgiveness, his healing, his rescue, his crowning love. Here not-forgetting is a deliberate command he gives himself, tied directly to the call to praise. Remembering God's goodness and blessing him are really the same movement. Worship, the passage shows, runs on a refusal to let God's kindnesses drop out of mind.
narratives.variation_note: A NOT-forget disposition addressed by the self to its own soul and fused with praise ('bless the LORD... forget not his benefits') - memory as the engine of worship, contrasting the enacted God-forgetting that elsewhere breeds sin.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember (zakar)' and the type (102) is action. The bearer (105) is 'the faithful' and the operation (106) is 'remember', but the target (107) is distinctive: 'to do God's commandments' - remembrance aimed not at recollection for its own sake but at doing. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. As with the neighbouring 103 readings, the record transposes locus/coupling: coupling (112) reads 'external:god' and locus (116) reads 'paired with keeping the covenant' - together binding the remembering to covenant-keeping. The process runs God's everlasting love on those who fear him (v17) -> those who keep his covenant -> AND remember to do his commandments. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured, the doing itself the point. The discovery note (114) reads v18 as the mindful obedience of the faithful, memory issuing in doing. Role (115) is characteristic. As an inner-being movement this is memory as practical: remembrance that terminates in action, the faithful holding God's commandments in mind precisely in order to keep them - memory and obedience welded so that to remember is to do.
narratives.story: The poem describes the faithful as those who keep God's covenant and remember to do his commandments. Here remembering is thoroughly practical - not just calling something to mind but holding it in mind in order to act on it. Memory and obedience are bound together, so that remembering God's commands means actually keeping them. This shows a kind of remembering whose whole aim is doing.
narratives.variation_note: Distinct target: remembrance aimed 'to do God's commandments' - memory that terminates in obedience (welded to covenant-keeping), rather than recollection of God's deeds or the self recalling God in distress.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember (zakar)' and the type (102) is action. The operation (106) is 'remember', a summons to worship. The bearer (105) is 'the worshippers' - the congregation called to praise - and the target (107) is 'God's wondrous works'. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Record transposes locus/coupling: coupling (112) reads 'external:god' and locus (116) 'paired with the wondrous works and covenant' - binding the remembering to the covenant-recital that follows (vv8-11, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, the land). The process runs the call to give thanks and seek God (vv1-4) -> REMEMBER his wondrous works -> the hinge into the covenant history. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured. The discovery note (114) reads v5 as the deliberate recalling of God's deeds, the hinge into the covenant-recital. Role (115) is characteristic. As an inner-being movement this is memory as corporate liturgy: the congregation commanded to recall God's deeds together, remembrance functioning as the doorway from praise into the rehearsal of covenant history - memory that founds a people's shared identity.
narratives.story: The congregation is called to give thanks, seek God, and remember the wonderful things he has done. Here remembering is a shared act of worship, a summons to the whole people to recall God's deeds together. It opens straight into the long retelling of God's promises to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. This is memory as public worship, the doorway into a people's shared story.
narratives.variation_note: A corporate, liturgical summons to remember (bearer 'the worshippers'), functioning as the hinge into covenant-recital - remembrance founding shared identity, distinct from the private, distress-driven recalls of the lament psalms.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember (zakar, negated)' and the type (102) is action. This is a NOT-remember: the operation (106) is 'fail to remember'. The bearer (105) is 'the fathers' and the target (107) is 'God's steadfast love'. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Record transposes locus/coupling: coupling (112) reads 'internal:ib-state' and locus (116) 'paired with not considering, and with rebelling' - binding the memory-failure to not-considering (v7a) and to the rebellion at the Red Sea. The process runs the fathers in Egypt -> not considering God's wondrous works -> NOT remembering the abundance of his steadfast love -> rebelling by the sea. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured, the rebellion carried by the coupling. The discovery note (114) reads v7 as the forgetting of God's love that bred rebellion. Role (115) is characteristic. As an inner-being movement this is memory-failure as the seedbed of rebellion: the abundance of God's love dropping from mind, and with it any restraint - the interior collapse (not-considering, not-remembering) that issues directly in revolt.
narratives.story: The poem recalls that the fathers, even in Egypt, did not take God's wonders to heart and did not remember how abundant his love was - and so they rebelled at the Red Sea. Here failing to remember is the root of revolt: once God's steadfast love slips from mind, nothing holds them back. The not-remembering is bound to a not-considering and to open rebellion. It shows how losing hold of God's love can lead straight into defiance.
narratives.variation_note: A NOT-remember whose object is God's STEADFAST LOVE (not his deeds), and which is coupled directly to rebellion - memory-failure as the seedbed of revolt, distinct from the forgetting of works elsewhere in the psalm.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'forget (shakach)' and the type (102) is action - a past-tense deed. The distinctive mark is speed: this is the SWIFT forgetting. The bearer (105) is 'the fathers' and the operation (106) is 'forget', target (107) 'God's works'. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Record transposes locus/coupling: coupling (112) reads 'internal:ib-state' and locus (116) 'paired with not waiting for his counsel' - binding the forgetting to impatience. The process runs the redemption at the sea and the song of praise (vv10-12) -> they SOON forgot his works -> they did not wait for his counsel -> wanton craving and testing God (vv14). Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - though the note foregrounds the speed, it is registered in the discovery, not as a graded intensity. The discovery note (114) reads v13 as the swift forgetting, the song of v12 dying within days. Role (115) is characteristic. As an inner-being movement this is the fragility of grateful memory: praise sung at the sea evaporates almost at once, forgetting so rapid that gratitude cannot outlast the crisis that provoked it - memory that will not hold.
narratives.story: No sooner had the people sung God's praise at the sea than they forgot what he had done and stopped waiting for his guidance. The striking thing here is the speed: the song of thanks died within days. This swift forgetting led straight into reckless craving and putting God to the test. It shows how fragile grateful memory can be - praise in a crisis that evaporates almost as soon as the danger passes.
narratives.variation_note: The SWIFT forgetting ('they soon forgot') - distinguished from the other 106 forgettings by its speed: gratitude sung at the sea evaporates within days, memory that cannot outlast the crisis that provoked it.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'forget (shakach)' and the type (102) is action. This is the gravest specimen: the thing forgotten is God himself, named as Saviour. The bearer (105) is 'the fathers' and the operation (106) is 'forget', target (107) 'God their Saviour'. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Record transposes locus/coupling: coupling (112) reads 'internal:ib-state' and locus (116) 'paired with worshiping the calf' - binding the forgetting to idolatry. The process runs the glory of God exchanged for the image of an ox (v20) -> they forgot God their Saviour -> who had done great things in Egypt. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured. The discovery note (114) reads v21 as the forgetting of the very God who redeemed them. Role (115) is characteristic. As an inner-being movement this is forgetting at its most total: not merely losing God's deeds from mind but losing the Redeemer himself, the memory-void directly coupled to idolatry - the calf rushing in to fill the place the forgotten Saviour had held. Read without valence-bias, this is the family's nadir: memory-loss as the interior condition that makes idolatry possible.
narratives.story: Having made a golden calf and bowed to it, the people forgot God their Saviour, who had done such great things for them in Egypt. This is forgetting at its worst - not just losing sight of what God did, but losing hold of the Rescuer himself. And into the empty place left by the forgotten Saviour rushes the idol. It shows how forgetting God is the very thing that makes false worship possible.
narratives.variation_note: The gravest 'forgot': the object is God himself as Saviour (not merely his works), coupled directly to calf-worship - forgetting as the interior void that idolatry rushes to fill, the family's nadir.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember (zakar, negated)' and the type (102) is disposition. This is a NOT-remember borne by the ENEMY: the operation (106) is 'fail to remember'. The bearer (105) is 'the enemy' and the target (107) is 'to show kindness'. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Record transposes locus/coupling: coupling (112) reads 'internal:ib-state' and locus (116) 'paired with pursuing the poor' - binding the memory-failure to cruelty. The process runs the enemy's settled disposition -> not remembering to show kindness -> pursuing the poor, needy, and brokenhearted to death. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured, the lethal cruelty carried by the coupling. The discovery note (114) reads v16 as the ground of the whole curse: the enemy's forgetting of mercy. Role (115) is characteristic. Read without valence-bias (directive 5), this is the memory-family working in the wicked's interior: not-remembering-to-show-kindness as a fixed orientation that issues in persecution to the death - here forgetting mercy is not weakness but the very engine of malice, and the psalm makes it the justifying ground of its imprecation.
narratives.story: The poem builds its curse on one charge against the enemy: he did not remember to show kindness, but hounded the poor and needy and broken-hearted to death. Here failing to remember is a fixed cruelty of the heart - mercy dropped so completely from mind that it never restrains the hand. The forgetting of kindness is bound directly to the killing pursuit of the helpless. It is named as the root of the man's whole malice and the ground of the judgment called down on him.
narratives.variation_note: A NOT-remember borne by the ENEMY and typed as disposition: the object is 'to show kindness', and the memory-failure is the ENGINE of malice (coupled to pursuing the poor to death) - forgetting in the wicked's interior, not the faithful's, and the ground of the psalm's curse.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'forget (shakach, negated)' and the type (102) is disposition. This anchor stands for the whole FORGET-arc of Psalm 119 (recurring at vv61, 93, 109, 141, 153, 176). The operation (106) is 'not forget (or, of foes, forget)' - the record itself flags the arc's two poles: the psalmist vows never to forget God's word, while the foes are those who do. The bearer (105) is the psalmist and the target (107) is 'God's word/precepts'. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) is 'paired with the whole FORGET-arc of the psalm' (inferred): across the acrostic, not-forgetting recurs as a sustained disposition through affliction, snares, smallness, and near-death. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured. The discovery note (114) reads v16 as the guarded memory joined to delight ('I will delight in your statutes; I will not forget your word'). Role (115) is characteristic, locus (116) external:god. As an inner-being movement this is not-forgetting as a lifelong devotional posture: memory of God's word fused with delight and repeatedly reaffirmed under pressure - remembrance held not by feeling but by will, the recurrences (directive 9) showing the same vow renewed again and again across the psalm.
narratives.story: In the great psalm on God's law, the poet declares: I will delight in your word, and I will never forget it. This vow not to forget runs like a thread through the whole long poem, repeated again and again as he faces trouble, traps, contempt, and near-death. Here not-forgetting is a settled, lifelong devotion, memory of God's word bound together with delight in it and held firm by will rather than mood. The many repetitions show the same promise renewed under every kind of pressure.
narratives.variation_note: The anchor for Psalm 119's whole not-forget arc (recurs 6x): a sustained devotional disposition (not-forgetting God's word joined to delight), distinct from the single-occasion recalls elsewhere - held by will and renewed repeatedly under pressure. Its foes-pole surfaces separately at v139 (forget#8).

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember (zakar)' and the type (102) is action. The bearer (105) is the psalmist and the operation (106) is 'remember', target (107) 'God's word' - but the object as verse-fixed is God's NAME in the night (v55). Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) is 'paired within its char-arc across the psalm' (inferred): the remembering belongs to the wider devotional pattern of Psalm 119. The process runs the night -> remembering God's name -> keeping his law: memory issuing directly in obedience. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured. The discovery note (114) reads v55 as remembering God's name through the night. Role (115) is characteristic, locus (116) external:god. As an inner-being movement this is memory as nocturnal fidelity: like Psalm 63:6 the mind turns to God in the dark, but here the fruit named is law-keeping - remembering God's name and keeping his law joined as one, so that night-time remembrance is not merely comfort but the spur to obedience even in the dark hours.
narratives.story: In the night, the poet says, he remembers God's name - and keeps his law. Here remembering God is tied straight to obedience: calling God to mind in the dark leads him to hold onto God's commands. It is part of the steady devotion that runs through this long poem. Night-time remembering here is not just comfort but a spur to faithful living even when no one is watching.
narratives.variation_note: A night-remembering (like Psa 63:6) but here the fruit is law-keeping: remembering God's name issues directly in obedience, part of Psalm 119's sustained devotional arc rather than a standalone comfort.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'forget (shakach, negated)' and the type (102) is disposition. The operation (106) is 'not forget (or, of foes, forget)' and the bearer (105) is the psalmist, target (107) 'God's word/precepts'. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) is 'paired with the whole FORGET-arc of the psalm' (inferred), locus (116) external:god. The distinctive mark is the setting of endurance: memory held though the self is shrivelled. The process runs affliction (become like a wineskin in the smoke) -> yet NOT forgetting God's statutes. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured, though the imagery of the smoke-dried wineskin conveys extremity. The discovery note (114) reads v83 as memory kept though shrivelled by affliction. Role (115) is characteristic. As an inner-being movement this is not-forgetting as tenacity in suffering: the body and spirit dried out like a skin hung in smoke, yet the grip on God's word unbroken - remembrance surviving precisely where affliction has hollowed everything else, memory as the last thing to go.
narratives.story: The poet says he has become like a wineskin shrivelled and blackened in the smoke - dried out by suffering - and yet he has not forgotten God's word. Here not-forgetting is sheer tenacity: everything else in him is worn away, but his hold on God's commands survives. Memory is the last thing to go, clinging on when the body and spirit are spent. It shows a faithfulness that endures precisely where affliction has hollowed the person out.
narratives.variation_note: Within Psalm 119's forget-arc, this reading foregrounds ENDURANCE: not-forgetting held though the self is shrivelled 'like a wineskin in the smoke' - memory as the last faculty to survive affliction, a tenacity-under-suffering colouring distinct from the delight-joined vow of v16.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'forget (shakach, negated)' and the type (102) is disposition. Distinctively, this is the FOES' pole of Psalm 119's forget-arc: the bearer (105) is 'the foes' and the operation (106) is 'not forget (or, of foes, forget)' - here the actual forgetting, done by the enemies. The target (107) is 'God's word/precepts'. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) is 'paired with the whole FORGET-arc of the psalm' (inferred), locus (116) external:god. The process runs the foes forgetting God's words -> the psalmist's zeal consuming him because of it. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured, though the psalmist's consuming zeal is the registered response. The discovery note (114) reads v139 as the foes' forgetting that stirs the psalmist's zeal. Role (115) is characteristic. As an inner-being movement this preserves the distinction (directive 8) from the psalmist's own not-forgetting: the SAME arc holds both poles - the devotee who will not forget and the foes who do - and here it is the foes' forgetting that becomes the object of the psalmist's grief and burning zeal, memory-failure in others provoking passion in the faithful self.
narratives.story: The poet's zeal burns him up, he says, because his enemies forget God's words. Here it is the foes who do the forgetting, and the psalmist's response is consuming passion - grief and zeal at seeing God's law ignored. This is the flip side of his own vow never to forget: the same concern for God's word makes him ache when others let it go. Other people's forgetting of God stirs a fierce inner fire in the faithful.
narratives.variation_note: The FOES' pole of Psalm 119's forget-arc (bearer 'the foes'), the enacted forgetting that counterpoints the psalmist's own not-forgetting vow (v16) - here memory-failure in others provokes the psalmist's consuming zeal.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember (zakar)' and the type (102) is action. The bearer (105) is 'the exiles' - a corporate memory - and the operation (106) is 'remember', target (107) 'Zion'. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) here carries a transposed datum 'internal:ib-state', and locus (116) reads 'paired with the weeping' - together binding the remembering to grief. The process runs exile by the waters of Babylon -> remembering Zion -> sitting down and weeping. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured, the weeping carried by the coupling. The discovery note (114) reads v1 as the memory that opens the grief, the lost home called to mind. Role (115) is characteristic. As an inner-being movement this is memory as the trigger of corporate mourning: the exiles' recollection of Zion is what breaks them into tears - like Psalm 42's wounding recall, remembrance of a lost sacred place deepens the pain of separation, memory and weeping welded as a single motion of the displaced community.
narratives.story: By the rivers of Babylon the exiles sat down and wept when they remembered Zion, their lost home. Here remembering is what opens the grief - the moment the memory of the city rises, the tears come. It is a shared sorrow, a whole displaced people mourning together. Recalling the beloved place they have lost does not comfort them; it breaks their hearts.
narratives.variation_note: A CORPORATE remembering (bearer 'the exiles') that TRIGGERS mourning (coupled to weeping) - like Psa 42:4 memory of a lost sacred place wounds; distinct from the ordered-love remembering of Jerusalem at v6 in the same psalm.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember (zakar)' and the type (102) is action. Distinctively, the operation (106) is remembrance as ORDERED LOVE: the bearer (105) is the psalmist and the target (107) is 'Jerusalem above all joy' - the city bound to the very top of his hierarchy of joys. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) carries the transposed 'internal:ib-state', and locus (116) reads 'paired with setting Jerusalem above his highest joy' - binding the remembering to a self-imposed ranking of loves. The process runs the vow -> if I do not remember you -> if I do not set Jerusalem above my highest joy -> (the self-curse of the tongue sticking). Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured, the ranking itself the point. The discovery note (114) reads v6 as the operation of ordered love: the city bound to the top of all the psalmist's joys. Role (115) is characteristic. As an inner-being movement this is memory as the guardian of priorities: to remember Jerusalem is precisely to keep it enthroned above every other joy - remembrance here is not passive recall but an act of ranking one's loves, the will fixing what shall stand highest.
narratives.story: The poet vows to remember Jerusalem by setting it above his very highest joy - and calls down a curse on himself if he fails. Here remembering is not just calling the city to mind but keeping it enthroned at the top of everything he loves. It is an act of ordering his loves, deciding what matters most. To remember Jerusalem, for him, means never letting anything else take first place.
narratives.variation_note: Distinct from the exiles' grief-remembering at v1: here remembering is ORDERED LOVE - the psalmist vowing to set Jerusalem above his highest joy, memory as an act of ranking his loves rather than a trigger of tears.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'forget (shakach, negated)' and the type (102) is disposition. The operation (106) is 'not forget' and the bearer (105) is the psalmist, target (107) 'Jerusalem'. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located. Coupling (112) carries the transposed 'internal:ib-state', and locus (116) reads 'paired with the hand failing if he forgets' - binding the not-forgetting to a self-curse on the hand. The process runs the vow -> if I forget you, Jerusalem -> let my right hand forget its skill. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured. The discovery note (114) reads v5 as the operation of self-binding memory: the vow to hold Jerusalem so fast that forgetting would be self-mutilation. Role (115) is characteristic. As an inner-being movement this is not-forgetting made into a self-binding oath: the psalmist stakes his own hand on his memory, so that to forget the city would be to lose his very skill - remembrance held not merely as devotion but as a vow enforced by the threat of self-loss, memory guarded by staking the self against its failure.
narratives.story: The poet swears: if I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand lose its skill. Here not-forgetting is turned into a binding oath - he stakes his own hand, his very ability, on holding the city in memory. To forget would be to cripple himself. This shows memory guarded so fiercely that the person ties his own well-being to never letting the beloved place slip from mind.
narratives.variation_note: The vow-side of the self-curse (bearer the psalmist, 'not forget'): distinguished from its pair forget#10 by being the CONDITION - the intent not to forget Jerusalem - whereas forget#10 is the penalty enacted on the hand. Preserving the two as distinct (directive 8).

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'forget (shakach)' and the type (102) is action - here the forgetting is transferred to the hand as a penalty. The distinctive mark is the bearer (105): 'the psalmist's hand', not the psalmist himself - the self-curse personified in a body part. The operation (106) is 'forget its skill' and the target (107) is 'if he forgets Jerusalem' (the condition). Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - and yet the reading is precisely about a bodily member, so the 'none' seat sits in tension with the hand as the locus of penalty: the skill is not seated as an inner organ-function but assigned as forfeit. Coupling (112) carries the transposed 'internal:ib-state', locus (116) 'paired with the vow not to forget'. The process runs the condition (if he forgets Jerusalem) -> the hand forgetting its skill: forgetting punished by forgetting, the mental lapse answered by a manual one. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - no degree measured. The discovery note (114) reads v5 as the self-curse that seals the vow: may the very hand lose its cunning if the memory of Zion lapses. Role (115) is characteristic. As an inner-being movement this shows memory and skill bound as one worth: the interior lapse of forgetting is imagined to strike the hand, the self willing its own maiming as the price of any disloyalty of memory - preserving the distinction from forget#9 (the vow), this is the penalty it invokes.
narratives.story: To seal his vow, the poet says: if I forget Jerusalem, let my right hand forget how to play. Here the forgetting is thrown onto his own hand as a punishment - a mental lapse answered by a crippled skill. He willingly imagines his own maiming as the price of any disloyalty of memory. Forgetting the city and losing his craft are bound together as a single loss.
narratives.variation_note: The penalty-side of the self-curse (bearer 'the psalmist's hand', enacted 'forget its skill'): distinguished from its pair forget#9 (the vow/condition) - here forgetting is transferred to the hand as forfeit, mental lapse answered by manual loss. The two are kept distinct (directive 8).

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'remember to rouse faith' and the type (102) is cognition - and this reading is unusually explicit about memory's function. The bearer (105) is the psalmist and the operation (106) is 'deliberately recalling former days, God's deeds and works, to reignite trust'. The target (107) is 'active-recall' and the coupling (112) is 'remember-God's-deeds' - the process names its own purpose: against desolation, the self chooses memory to feed faith. Source (103) absent; seat (104) 'none' - not organ-located; locus (116) internal:ib-state. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) all absent - the reading does not grade the effort or trace a measured outcome, though the aim (reignited trust) is built into the operation. The discovery note (114) reads v5 as: against the desolation the self chooses memory, feeding faith on God's past acts (spirit fainting, heart appalled, v4). Role (115) is characteristic. As an inner-being movement this is the fullest statement of memory-as-remedy in the family: with the spirit fainting and the heart appalled, the psalmist deliberately recalls the days of old and meditates on God's works precisely in order to rouse trust - like Psalm 77:11 memory is chosen medicine, the will turning to the past to overturn a present despair.
narratives.story: With his spirit failing and his heart in dismay, the poet deliberately calls to mind the days of old and dwells on all that God has done. He does this on purpose, to rekindle his trust - memory used as a cure for despair. Rather than sink under his troubles, he chooses to feed his faith on God's past deeds. Here remembering is a deliberate strategy of the soul: reach back to what God has done in order to find courage now.
narratives.variation_note: The most explicit memory-as-remedy reading (sense 'remember to rouse faith', operation names its own purpose): like Psa 77:11 memory is deliberately chosen against despair, but here the aim - reigniting trust - is built into the operation itself, locus internal:ib-state.
